units.source_text: 「俗話說‘財竭緣盡’，其實，這句話被解釋反了。

en.t: People say, 'When the money runs out, the relationship ends,' but actually that saying has been explained backwards.

units.source_text: 其意是，並非錢用完了，男人就會被女人甩掉。

en.t: What it means is not that once the money is gone, the man will be cast off by the woman.

units.source_text: 而是男人沒有了錢，自己就會意志消沉，一蹶不振，

en.t: Rather, when a man loses his money, he loses heart on his own and cannot recover,

units.source_text: 連笑的氣力都沒有，而且也會慢慢變得莫名怪僻與暴躁，

en.t: he no longer has even the strength to laugh, and little by little he becomes strangely warped and irritable,

units.source_text: 最終破罐子破摔，近乎瘋狂地拋棄女人。

en.t: until in the end he gives up in desperation and abandons the woman almost madly.

units.source_text: 《金澤大辭林》上就是這麼解釋的。

en.t: That is how it is explained in the Kanazawa Great Dictionary.

units.source_text: 真可憐啊，我也懂得那種心情。」

en.t: How pitiful. I understand that feeling too."

units.source_text: 我確實說過這樣的蠢話，也記得常子笑噴的場面。

en.t: I certainly said some such foolish thing, and I also remember Tsuneko bursting out laughing.
